meta.title: Operation of Conventional Coating Pan in Pharmaceutics Laboratory

sections.purpose: To apply sugar or film coatings to tablet cores to improve palatability, provide moisture protection, control drug release, and achieve a desired appearance as part of solid dosage form manufacturing.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutics laboratory for coating of tablet cores with sugar coating, film coating, or enteric coating solutions as part of formulation development and scale-up studies.
procedure: Inspect the coating pan, spray system, and air supply for cleanliness and correct assembly.
Warm the coating pan to 40–50°C using the hot air supply for 10–15 minutes before loading tablets.
Weigh the tablet cores accurately; record the pre-coating weight.
Load tablet cores into the rotating coating pan — typically 60–75% of the pan capacity.
Set the pan rotation speed: 20–40 RPM for sugar coating; 10–20 RPM for film coating — tablets should cascade freely without flying.
Prepare the coating solution as per the formulation: dissolve sugar, film polymer (HPMC, EC, Eudragit), or enteric polymer in the specified solvent system.
For film coating: begin applying the coating solution by ladle or spray gun in small portions, pausing between applications to allow drying.
Blow warm air (40–60°C) continuously onto the tablet bed during coating.
Monitor tablet weight gain at regular intervals — the required coating weight gain is specified in the formulation (typically 2–5% for film coating; 30–50% for sugar coating).
Observe tablet surfaces: coated tablets should be smooth, uniformly coloured, and non-adherent.
After achieving target weight gain, apply a polishing coat (beeswax/carnauba wax blend) if required.
Cool the tablets by blowing room-temperature air for 10–15 minutes before removing from pan.
Remove tablets, weigh, and inspect for coating defects: peeling, orange peel texture, colour variation, logo bridging.
Package coated tablets in moisture-proof containers immediately.
Record coating solution composition, weight gain at each stage, temperature, and pan speed in the batch manufacturing record.
precautions: Ensure tablets have adequate hardness (minimum 5–6 kp) before coating — soft tablets crumble in the rotating pan.
Maintain correct inlet air temperature and dew point — too hot causes film cracking; too cool causes picking and sticking.
Do not overload the pan — insufficient cascading causes uneven coating.
For organic solvent-based film coating: work in a fume hood; ensure solvent vapour extraction is functioning.
Use grounded equipment and non-sparking tools for flammable solvent coating solutions.
Inspect spray nozzles for clogging at regular intervals during operation — a clogged nozzle creates coating-free zones.
Clean the coating pan immediately after use — dried coating solution is very difficult to remove.
